implementation_notes: Java records (16+) supply canonical accessors, equals/hashCode and shallow immutability but no copy-with, so the update is hand-written: a wither returns a new instance built from the canonical constructor - `Person withCity(String city) { return new Person(name, city); }` - and a nested update chains the withers, which is exactly the copy cascade the lens pattern exists to centralise. A reusable `Lens<S, A>` must likewise be hand-written as a functional interface with `get`, `set` and an `andThen` default (annotation processors such as hkj-optics generate them); that classic composed form pays off only when many call sites update the same deep field, because records give no way to declare the setter once and share it.
pitfalls: Records are only shallowly immutable: a `List`/`Map`/array component stays mutable, so a wither that reuses it shares state between the old and the new record - wrap with List.copyOf/Map.copyOf.
Every wither allocates a new instance per level; deep chains in hot paths show up in allocation profiles, which is why "just use records" and "use lenses everywhere" both fail there.
A leaked mutable array component also breaks the record's equals/hashCode contract, because hashCode is derived from the array reference.
